source_text:
Epistula ad Joannem Hierosolymitanum
Πρὸς Ἰωάννην τὸν Αἰλείας ἐπίσκοπον ἐπιγεγραμμένη ἐπιστολή.
Τῷ αἰδεσιμωτάτῳ ἀδελφῷ πάπᾳ Ἰωάννῃ Ἐπιφάνιος ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Κυρίῳ
χαίρειν.
Ἔδει ἡμᾶς ἀγαπητὲ μὴ τῇ οἰήσει τῶν κλήρων φέρεσθαι, ἀλλὰ ... 282 ... φησὶ
γὰρ ἡ θεία γραφή· (Paul. ad. Cor. 10, 10) μηδὲ γογγύζετε καθάπερ τινὲς ἐγόγγυσαν
καὶ ἀπώλοντο ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ (cf. 10, 9 ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ἀπώλοντο) ... ...
thought_title: Greeting and warning against pride and grumbling
orientation: Epiphanius opens his letter to John of Jerusalem with a formal greeting, then immediately warns him not to be carried away by pride of office, citing Scripture against grumbling.
pass_a_gloss: A letter inscribed to John the bishop of Aelia. To the most reverend brother father John, Epiphanius bishop, in the Lord, greetings. It was necessary for us, beloved, not to be carried away by the pride of offices, but ... 282 ... For the divine Scripture says: (Paul to the Corinthians 10:10) 'Do not grumble, just as some grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer' (cf. 10:9 'they were destroyed by the serpents') ... ...

choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary renderings 'pride' for οἴησις and 'office' for κλῆρος, keeping the plural to reflect the source's range of clerical ranks.
Middle/passive infinitive with the sense of being swept along by an impulse; preserves the passive force of the Greek.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering 'grumble' for γογγύζω and keeps the negated imperative force of μηδέ.
Literal rendering of the agent phrase; 'destroyer' matches the Greek noun's sense of one who destroys.
Renders the honorific title literally as used in the source for a bishop, without modern denominational overtones.

bible_refs.note: μηδὲ γογγύζετε καθάπερ τινὲς ἐγόγγυσαν καὶ ἀπώλοντο ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ

pass_b_english: To the most reverend brother and father John, Epiphanius, bishop, sends greetings in the Lord.

We ought not, beloved, to be carried away by the pride of office, but ... For the divine Scripture says through the apostle: “Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer” (1 Corinthians 10:10).
notes: The source has a lacuna marked by '... 282 ...' after 'ἀλλὰ', indicating missing text in the manuscript.

problems.why: 'πάπᾳ' means 'papa/pope', not 'fellow bishop'; changes John's title.
problems.fix: To the most reverend brother and papa John, Epiphanius sends greetings in the Lord.
problems.ruling: πάπᾳ means 'papa,' not 'fellow bishop'; English adds 'fellow bishop' not in source.

problems.quote: We ought not, beloved, to be carried away by the pride of office.
problems.why: Missing 'bishop' in Epiphanius's self-identification; 'ἐπίσκοπος' is in source.
problems.fix: Epiphanius, bishop, sends greetings in the Lord.
problems.ruling: ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Κυρίῳ χαίρειν omitted; Epiphanius's title 'bishop' and greeting lost.

edits.old: To the most reverend brother and fellow bishop John, Epiphanius sends greetings in the Lord.
edits.new: To the most reverend brother and papa John, Epiphanius, bishop, sends greetings in the Lord.

fixed: The English already says 'Epiphanius sends greetings in the Lord' but omits 'bishop'; this is corrected in the edit.
The English 'fellow bishop' is not a valid rendering of 'πάπᾳ'; corrected to 'papa'.

problems.quote: We ought not, beloved, to be carried away by the pride of office.
problems.source_quote: Ἔδει ἡμᾶς ἀγαπητὲ μὴ τῇ οἰήσει τῶν κλήρων φέρεσθαι, ἀλλὰ ... 282 ...
problems.why: The 'but...' clause after 'not...but' is omitted with its content.
problems.fix: We ought not, beloved, to be carried away by the pride of office, but [text missing in source gap].
problems.ruling: Source has ἀλλὰ ... 282 ... introducing a contrast clause and content; English omits 'but' and following material entirely.

problems.source_quote: (Paul. ad. Cor. 10, 10) μηδὲ γογγύζετε καθάπερ τινὲς ἐγόγγυσαν καὶ ἀπώλοντο ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ (cf. 10, 9 ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ἀπώλοντο)
problems.why: The citation should note the allusion to 10:9 as marked in source with 'cf. 10, 9'.
problems.ruling: Source includes 'cf. 10, 9 ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ἀπώλοντο'; English omits this cross-reference, misleading the reader.

edits.old: We ought not, beloved, to be carried away by the pride of office. For the divine Scripture says:
edits.new: We ought not, beloved, to be carried away by the pride of office, but ... For the divine Scripture says:

problems.why: Same person addressed as 'papa' then 'your honor'; reader may miss continuity.
problems.fix: Use one title or gloss 'papa' as honorific.

problems.quote: Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer
problems.why: Cited as 1 Cor 10:10 with allusion to 10:9, but 'destroyer' language matches Exodus 12:23/Hebrews 11:28 more closely.
problems.fix: Verify citation; may conflate multiple texts.

edits.old: To the most reverend brother and papa John, Epiphanius, bishop, sends greetings in the Lord.
edits.new: To the most reverend brother and father John, Epiphanius, bishop, sends greetings in the Lord.

edits.old: “Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer” (1 Corinthians 10:10, with allusion to 10:9).
edits.new: “Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer” (1 Corinthians 10:10).

fixed: The 'papa' issue is real: 'papa' is a title of address for a bishop, not a name, and using 'papa John' reads like a modern pizza chain. Changed to 'father John' to preserve the honorific sense while avoiding confusion.

The scripture citation issue is real: the source quotes 1 Corinthians 10:10 directly, and the 'destroyer' language is part of that verse in the Greek text. The allusion to 10:9 is already present in the source's parenthetical note but is not part of the direct quotation. Removed the 'with allusion to 10:9' from the English citation to match the source's direct quotation.

problems.quote: Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer
problems.why: Scripture quoted without identifying speaker (Paul/1 Corinthians).

edits.old: For the divine Scripture says: “Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer” (1 Corinthians 10:10).
edits.new: For the divine Scripture says through the apostle: “Do not grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer” (1 Corinthians 10:10).

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'office' for κλῆρος, but 'papa' for πάπᾳ is not in brief.
last_rejected.fix: To the most reverend brother and papa John
last_rejected.ruling: πάπᾳ is transliterated as 'papa,' a standard rendering for this honorific; no glossary issue with κλῆρος is affected.
